subject: Private endpoint egress: allowlist approach and firewall scoping proposal
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: security@helixhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress: allowlist approach and firewall scoping proposal

Hi Paul / Helix security team,

Thanks for taking the time on the integration call last week. We're kicking off the egress planning for the private Redwood runtime we'll stand up inside Helix's VPC. We want to be explicit about the minimum inbound/outbound controls needed so your networking team can scope firewall rules and audit controls.

Summary of what we need from Helix to complete our onboarding checklist:
- Which outbound enforcement model do you prefer for tenant traffic from the private runtime? (static NAT IPs, NAT pool with static control-plane, or SNI-based allowlist)
- Do you require TLS interception / SNI inspection for outbound flows? If so, provide certificate pinning constraints and whether mTLS is acceptable for control-plane endpoints.
- Is there an internal proxy (IP/port) that all outbound traffic must flow through? If yes, give IP, port, and whether authentication (basic/Bearer/mTLS) is required.
- Whether Helix will supply a short list of egress IPs to allow, or if you prefer us to publish a dynamic FQDN set (we can provide both).

Attached is a suggested starting set (redwood-egress-suggested.csv) enumerating control-plane and optional runtime egress FQDNs and ports. We're proposing a hybrid: static control-plane IPs for observability/auth, and customer-managed NAT IPs for inference-worker egress to make audit logs cleaner.

Can you confirm who on your side will take point for the firewall ACLs and an ETA on the rule window? We're aiming to have the deployment acceptance test run the week of Jul 6 if possible.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-egress-suggested.csv (CSV stub, columns: role, hostname, fqdn, port, proto, note)

From: Paul Rivera <paul.rivera@helixhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: allowlist approach and firewall scoping proposal

Neha —

Thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: we have an org-wide perimeter that prefers static IP allowlists for auditability. That said, we are evaluating SNI-only controls for some SaaS partners to reduce ops churn.

Questions:
- If Redwood publishes FQDNs only, can we get a stable docs page and an IP provenance SLA? We need assurance that changes are announced 14 days ahead of rotation.
- What's Redwood's recommended frequency for ephemeral inference egress IP rotation if we go NAT-pool route? Our security team tends to object if IP sets rotate more frequently than 30 days.

I'll loop in our network lead (security@helixhealth.com) separately — they're out for most of today but available tomorrow.

Paul
Head of IT Security, Helix Health

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: allowlist approach and firewall scoping proposal

Neha / Marissa —

For internal ops planning and to help the Helix team, here's a concise set of scoping decisions we recommend (we can provide a JSON manifest or CSV for handoff):

1) Minimum allowlist entries (customer-facing):
   - Control-plane API (static) — 3 IPs: 52.33.42.10, 52.33.42.11, 52.33.42.12 TCP/443 (used for management, billing, metrics ingestion)
   - Healthcheck & telemetry endpoints — same control-plane IPs over 443

2) Inference worker egress options (choose one):
   A) Customer-managed NAT (preferred): workers egress through your NAT IP(s). Benefits: full packet-level audit, no outbound IP rotation from Redwood network.
   B) Redwood-managed NAT pool: we can provide an allowlist of ephemeral IPs. Recommend rotation window 30–90 days (default 60). If Helix selects this, we must include a 14-day change notice SLA.
   C) SNI / FQDN-only model: acceptable for low-compliance workloads, but problematic for DPI requirements and some auditors.

3) TLS/SNI considerations:
   - We support mTLS on the control-plane; recommend mTLS for any auth-sensitive control endpoints.
   - For inference egress, we strongly prefer no TLS interception; if Helix requires TLS inspection, we need the interception certs added to Redwood's runtime trust store (detailed steps in the attached checklist).

4) Firewall rules snippets to hand to netops (sample):
   - ALLOW TCP 52.33.42.10/32:443 # redwood-control-1
   - ALLOW TCP 52.33.42.11/32:443 # redwood-control-2
   - ALLOW TCP <customer-nat-ip>/32:443 # inference egress (customer-managed)

I'll draft a short CSV mapping to make it easy for them to import. Jonas will own the final rule generation for our acceptance test.

—David
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: allowlist approach and firewall scoping proposal

Paul / team —

Thanks for the quick note. Based on Helix's preference for static allowlists, here's the hybrid proposal we recommend so your auditors have clean traceability while keeping ops overhead low:

Proposal (hybrid - recommended):
- Control plane: Redwood publishes 3 static IPs (see David's list) used for management, telemetry, and auth. These are short list entries for your perimeter firewall.
- Inference workers: Helix will provide 1–3 customer NAT IPs that the workers will egress through (customer-managed NAT). That gives you packet-level audit and ensures IPs are stable as you prefer.
- Change management: for Redwood-managed IPs (control-plane) we commit to a 30-day notice for rotation and a weekly status page. For ephemeral inference pools (if used later) we recommend no more frequent than 60-day rotation; we will include a 14-day change notice.
- TLS inspection: we prefer no interception; if Helix must inspect, we'll require the CA cert and a maintenance window to roll trust stores (see egress-proofing-checklist.pdf attached).

Next actions:
1) Helix to confirm the NAT IPs (or confirm they will use Redwood-managed NAT) and provide staging firewall window (2-4 hour block).
2) Helix to confirm whether DPI/SNI inspection will be on the path.
3) Redwood to send a final CSV of allowlist rows and a short runbook for acceptance testing (we'll deliver by Thu Jun 25).

Attachments: helix-egress-safelist.xlsx; egress-proofing-checklist.pdf

If this works, Marissa/David and I will schedule the acceptance test slot.

Best,
Neha
